title: Building a cozy pixel-art village with Codex — especially happy with how the water turned out
author: beardeer
selftext:
**Building a cozy pixel-art village with Codex — especially happy with how the water turned out**

A little visual update on a witch game I’m building with Codex. The direction is cozy rural fantasy: golden leaves, plum-colored roofs, warm shop windows, and a stream running through the village.

The water is probably my favorite part right now. Little cascades spill between the rocks, foam breaks up downstream, and reflections move across the surface. In the rain, ripples interrupt the water and lantern light catches the wet stones. At dusk, the same stream picks up cooler blues and little streaks of warm light.

It’s surprisingly easy to lose time just watching it.

A bit about how we made it: the game runs in the browser, using a custom WebGL renderer with 2D pixel characters in a 3D environment. Codex helped build and refine the scene geometry, shaders, lighting, foliage, and water effects.

The workflow has been very visual: start with reference images for sunshine, rain, and dusk, render the actual game, compare screenshots, then make specific changes. Sometimes that meant changing colors; other times it meant rebuilding tree branches, adjusting how foam appears and fades, or making reflections respond better to the camera.

Keeping the three lighting conditions together throughout development helped the whole scene feel more consistent.

Sharing a few shots and the stream in all three conditions. Pretty happy with this little corner of the world.
